sections.h2: Where does an Anderson County deed get filed?
sections.html:
It gets filed at the Anderson County Clerk's counter, 100 S Main St, Lawrenceburg, KY 40342. Recording there is what makes a conveyance effective against later purchasers who had no notice and against the grantor's creditors (KRS 382.110(1)).

Lawrenceburg is the seat and only city. The General Assembly approved the county on January 16, 1827, cutting it from parts of Franklin, Washington and Mercer. Most sellers never visit the counter themselves. A closing attorney or title agent takes the signed deed over, pays the clerk, and the stamped original comes back by mail a little later.

sections.h2: What does the local market look like for someone selling here?
sections.html:
About 25,225 people lived in Anderson County in mid-2025, up from 23,852 in the 2020 count. Seven counties touch it: Franklin, Woodford, Mercer, Washington, Nelson, Spencer and Shelby. It belongs to the Frankfort micropolitan area, and the mean trip to work runs 30.4 minutes.

  • Typical owner-occupied house value, 2020 to 2024: $225,100.
  • Homes occupied by their owners: 77.6 percent, across 9,653 households.
  • Housing units counted in July 2025: 10,652.
  • Monthly owner costs at the midpoint: $1,391 with a mortgage, $411 without.
  • Household income at the midpoint: $74,488. Monthly rent at the midpoint: $927.

Owners far outnumber renters here, so most deeds the clerk sees record ordinary house sales and refinance paperwork.

The county spans about 202 square miles and lists 25 named places, among them Alton, Glensboro, McBrayer and Stringtown. A parcel in any of them is recorded in the same Lawrenceburg books, so the village name on a mailing address changes nothing about where the deed goes. Since 2020 the population has climbed about 5.6 percent.

sections.h2: What has to be written into the deed?
sections.html:
KRS 382.135 bars the clerk from filing a deed that lacks certain items, so a quick check before closing saves a return trip.

  • Both parties' full names and mailing addresses.
  • The full consideration stated in words or figures.
  • An in-care-of address for that year's property tax bill.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate from the seller and buyer that the stated price is the whole price. For a gift, the certificate says so and gives an estimated fair cash value.

KRS 382.110 adds a title-source rule. The deed has to name the earlier deed by office, book, page and recording date, or say how the seller came to own the land if it passed by inheritance. When a house came through a will or without one, the personal representative files an affidavit listing each heir, each parcel and its value with the clerk before the estate is closed.

sections.h2: What will the clerk charge me?
sections.html:
The clerk's posted schedule dates from January 1, 2020. Anything longer than five pages costs $3 for each additional page, and mortgages pay the same $3 only after page thirty. Separately, KRS 142.010 puts a $4 state tax on every real property conveyance, collected by the clerk and remitted to the state. Ask at the counter whether the quoted total already includes that $4.

A seller normally pays for one deed and perhaps one release, which makes clerk charges a small slice of closing costs.

sections.h2: How does the state transfer tax work in Anderson County?
sections.html:
The seller owes $0.50 per $500 of value in the deed, and any leftover part of $500 counts as a full unit (KRS 142.050). The clerk computes it and holds the deed back until it is paid. Try it on a sale at $225,100: that is 450 units plus a remainder, so 451 units and a tax of $225.50. The sum is only an illustration.

Where a deed is a gift or carries token consideration, the base is what the property would fetch on the open market. The clerk keeps 5 percent and forwards the balance each quarter to the county treasurer for the general fund. Exemptions include:

  • Transfers by foreclosure, or by voluntary surrender under a mortgage.
  • Spouse to spouse, including former spouses dividing property in a divorce.
  • Parent to child or grandparent to grandchild when only nominal money changes hands.
  • Deeds that only secure or release a debt, or fix an error in an earlier deed.
  • Conveyances after a tax sale, and partitions.

The clerk's records page lists an Exempt Transfer Affidavit, Form 71A245, for claiming one of these.

sections.h2: How far back do Anderson County land records go?
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages are indexed in CCLIX to 1966, and wills and marriages to 1797. Document images from January 2004 forward can mostly be pulled up online, while paper and microfilm reach into the 1700s.

Online access runs through eCCLIX, which requires an account from the vendor and charges for use. In the clerk's office anyone can read the same indexes and images without paying. The clerk also offers DocAlert, free email notices when a deed or mortgage is recorded under a name you register. Owners who live away from the county, or who hold rental houses, tend to like it for catching a fraudulent filing early.

sections.h2: What if the property tax was never paid?
sections.html:
The sheriff turns unpaid bills over to the clerk when business closes on April 15. At the clerk's counter, the Sheriff's Office says, a payer owes a 20 percent County Attorney fee, a 10 percent Clerk fee and 1 percent interest each month in addition to earlier penalties. By summer the debt can be sold to a private buyer.

KRS 134.015(5) lets the delinquency lien follow the land for up to eleven years, whoever holds title. A title agent will turn it up. Expect the payoff to be taken from the seller's proceeds. Before April 15 the Sheriff's Office at 208 S Main St, (502) 839-4021, accepts payment.

sections.h2: What is a sensible checklist before signing?
sections.html:
• Locate the deed you received and note its book and page.
  • Request the current bill and any older balance from the Sheriff's Office.
  • Ask the clerk whether any lien or lis pendens is recorded against the parcel.
  • Choose a mailing address for the buyer's tax bill and write it in.
  • Prepare an exemption affidavit if one of the transfer-tax exemptions fits.

The clerk's website also carries a delinquent-tax lookup, which is a quick way to see whether the parcel appears on the sale list. If you would rather sell in its present condition, ask for a written cash offer. The recording steps are the same once a price is agreed.

faqs.q: Do I record in Lawrenceburg if the house is outside the city?
faqs.a: Yes. One county clerk serves all of Anderson County. KRS 382.110 sends the deed to the clerk of the county containing the land, so a rural parcel still goes to the S Main Street office.

faqs.q: What is the minimum to record a deed?
faqs.a: The posted minimum is $50, plus $3 for each page after the fifth. KRS 142.010 also lays a $4 state tax on conveyances, so request a full total before writing a check.

faqs.q: Is the seller or the buyer responsible for the transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller, named as grantor, pays it. KRS 142.050 sets it at half a dollar per $500 of declared value, and the clerk collects it at the counter.

faqs.q: Can I look through old deeds without paying?
faqs.a: In person, yes. The clerk's records page says public records and indexes are free to view in the office. Online viewing through eCCLIX is a paid service.
No. KRS 142.050 exempts foreclosure transfers and voluntary surrenders under a mortgage. The lender then has 45 days from signing to file that deed with the clerk, per KRS 382.110.
